transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-10-07
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Acme CTO), Carlos Reyes (Acme ML Ops), Nina Patel (Acme Compliance)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: Short scoping call focused on POC data handling, redaction, and retention. Customer wants clarity on where prompts are stored, what logs Redwood retains, KMS integration, and how to run end-to-end benchmarks without exposing PHI/PII. Agreed next steps include security artifacts, benchmark plan, and scheduling an on-prem pilot week of 10/15.
Topics: PII handling, redaction, log retention, prompt storage, workload sizing, benchmark plan, success criteria, timelines
Action items: see metadata list above

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time. Quick round of intros - I'm Jordan, AE, and Priya's our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Maya (Acme): Hi all, Maya here. We'll start with a bit of background, we run ML infra for clinical triage, so lots of PHI concerns.
[00:20] Carlos (Acme): Carlos, I'm ML Ops, I own model infra and benchmarking.
[00:25] Nina (Acme): Nina, compliance, SOC2 owner for Acme.
[00:29] Priya (Redwood): Great, thanks. Goal for today is to scope the POC around data handling and retention decisions — basically we want to make sure you can run safe benchmarks without exposing real PHI and to confirm retention/KMS+redaction behavior.

[00:46] Maya: Yep. High level - we want a 3-week-ish POC, two parts: 1) functional — run 10k synthetic+sample traces to validate latency and quality, 2) compliance — confirm logs, redaction, and retention meet our internal policy.
[01:02] Jordan: Sounds good. Can you share the rough workload? QPS, tokens per request, concurrency?
[01:09] Carlos: Typical workload for the triage assistant is bursts up to 30 QPS, average request ~120 tokens, max context today 2k tokens but for triage we'll mostly be within 1k. Concurrent sessions about 25.
[01:21] Priya: Ok so for sizing we'd recommend a small dedicated pool for the POC — that'll give consistent latency; hosted can work but you'll see more variance. For benchmarks we'll do both hosted and Dedicatede — sorry — Dedicated (note: transcript tool slightly garbled).
[01:36] Maya: On the compliance side, main questions: where are prompts stored, are full transcripts kept, can you configure redaction for PII/PHI, and retention windows? Also KMS/HSM for keys?
[01:47] Priya: Great questions. Short answers: prompts and request payloads are logged by default for debugging and metrics, but customers can opt into disabling storage for request bodies and enable only aggregated telemetry. We support configurable retention policies per-tenant that can be set to 0 days (no retention) up to multi-year. We also support KMS integrations for envelope encryption of data at rest.
[02:12] Nina: When you say "redaction" — do you mean automatic PII scrubbing before storage and also in-flight masking? We need a deterministic way to prove PHI isn't persisted.
[02:22] Priya: We have two layers: 1) automatic redaction pipeline that strips or hashes detected PII before write to logs — it's ML-based so there is a small false negative rate; 2) a pre-send hook you can run client-side to remove or tokenise PHI before sending. For compliance, we recommend doing both: client-side tokenization for anything high-risk plus server-side redaction as defense-in-depth.
[02:46] Carlos: What's the false negative rate, roughly? We need thresholds for acceptance in POC.
[02:50] Priya: Our internal numbers for generic PII detection are around 98% recall on common patterns; PHI in clinical text is trickier — we can run a small eval on your sample anonymized dataset and report the metrics. For the POC success criteria we can define an acceptance threshold, e.g., <1% residual PII tokens or <0.5% exposures, whichever is easier to measure.
[03:12] Maya: That makes sense. Also, prompt storage — if we use tools/function-calls or chain-of-thought traces, are those stored in full? We don't want full prompts stored long-term.
[03:22] Priya: Prompts are part of request logs by default but retention is configurable. Additionally, we offer a "redact on write" option where we will replace detected strings with stable tokens before they ever hit disk. For the POC, we can set retention to 7 days and enable redact-on-write; then after benchmark runs we can purge logs.
[03:42] Jordan: Note for the POC we'll propose a process: provide a synthetic dataset that mirrors token distributions and prompt structure, run throughput and latency benchmarks, and run a redaction accuracy test on a small de-identified sample. We'll also do an integration test with your KMS.
[03:58] Carlos: How do you handle embeddings and vector DB logging? Those sometimes contain parts of prompts.
[04:04] Priya: We don't store embeddings unless you opt-in to vector retention. By default embeddings are ephemeral for serving; if you choose to persist them you control retention and encryption. For PII concerns, don't persist embeddings in the POC.
[04:18] Nina: Audit logs — we need immutable audit logs for who accessed what, and retention for those logs.
[04:24] Priya: Yes, audit logs are separate from request logs. We can export audit logs to your S3/Cloud Logging with a retention policy on your side; Redwood can keep a copy for the SLA window but we can configure minimal retention.
[04:35] Maya: On encryption, we need customer-managed keys — HSM preferred.
[04:39] Priya: We support KMS integrations with CMKs, and on private deployments HSM-backed keys are possible. For Hosted we do envelope encryption with keys you manage via KMS. We'll include a KMS integration playbook in the docs.
[04:53] Jordan: Let's talk success criteria for the POC — Maya, Carlos, what would success look like?
[04:58] Maya: For us success is threefold: (1) latency and throughput meet our SLOs — P95 under 450ms for typical requests and <50ms tail variance when on dedicated pool; (2) redaction/PII metrics meet compliance threshold — residual PII below 0.5% on sampled outputs; (3) integration with KMS + ability to configure retention and purge logs programmatically.
[05:22] Carlos: For performance we also want cost estimates at that QPS with typical token counts. Show us cost per 1M tokens for the Dedicated config.
[05:31] Priya: We will provide a cost model; for the POC we'll give an estimate and then a committed capacity quote if you go to Dedicated.
[05:38] Maya: Benchmarks — what's in scope? Latency (P50/P95/P99), throughput (max sustainable QPS), and quality (generation accuracy relative to our test set).
[05:47] Priya: Yes. We'll run synthetic replay of 10k requests that match your token distribution. We'll capture P50/P95/P99, CPU/GPU utilization, and cost numbers. For quality we'll run 1k labeled examples to measure precision/recall on key extraction tasks.
[06:03] Carlos: Can we run the benchmark in your private deployment? We might prefer VPC or on-prem to avoid any data egress issues.
[06:09] Priya: Absolutely. We can do the POC in a Private VPC deployment or an on-prem package if you want it air-gapped. That will add setup time — expect ~2 weeks for private environment provisioning. Hosted test can be done faster.
[06:24] Maya: Timeline? We need to align with a regulatory audit in late November, so ideally POC complete by mid-November.
[06:31] Jordan: So target finish mid-November — workable. Proposed schedule: week of 10/13 — final scoping + sign POC agreement; week of 10/20 — environment provisioning and KMS integration; week of 10/27 — run benchmarks; week of 11/03 — analysis and remediation; wrap up by 11/14. Does that timeline look ok?
[06:51] Carlos: That works if the provisioning can be parallelized. Also need to ensure a rollback plan if we find unacceptable PII exposures.
[06:58] Priya: Rollback plan: keep retention at 0-7 days during POC, redact-on-write enabled, and a purge run after each benchmark. If an exposure occurs we have an incident playbook — immediate log isolation, purge, and remediation with you. We'll add that to the security artifacts.
[07:16] Nina: We also need legal — data processing addendum, liability limits, and specifics on breach notification timelines.
[07:23] Jordan: We'll coordinate legal; I'll include standard DPA and SAs in the follow up email.
[07:27] Maya: One more technical: prompt caching and KV cache — will any cached KV material be persisted beyond retention?
[07:34] Priya: The runtime uses KV cache in-memory for performance. We don't persist KV caches to disk in hosted setups; in private/on-prem you'd control persistence. We'll confirm for Dedicated options.
[07:46] Carlos: For the accuracy tests on redaction, can Redwood run center-run detection on de-identified samples and provide confusion matrices?
[07:54] Priya: Yes, we'll run evaluation and deliver precision/recall, false positives/negatives, and a confusion matrix. We'll also surface examples of missed redactions with obfuscated content.
[08:05] Jordan: Ok to recap next steps — Jordan to share SOW, security artifacts, and SOC2 summary; Priya to deliver benchmark plan and sample dataset template; Nina to send compliance doc; schedule provisioning and pilot week of 10/15-10/20.
[08:20] Maya: Sounds good. Also please include a config snippet showing how to set retention to 7 days and enable redact-on-write.
[08:26] Priya: We'll include that in the docs.
[08:30] Maya: Anything else?
[08:32] Jordan: No, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the artifacts and confirm dates.
[08:36] Carlos: Thanks all.
[08:38] Nina: Thanks.

[End of transcript]

Notes: occasional transcription errors (e.g., "Dedicatede") present. References to shared artifacts: link to security pack (redwood.com/security-pack), sample benchmark sheet (link: drive.redwood/benchmark-acme), SOW template (link: drive.redwood/sow-template).
